memories.content: Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Clarify which stage of prototype fabrication or user study each requested resource is used for.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the personnel assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the equipment assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the time allocated to each procedure.
Verify that the planned number of formative evaluation iterations is feasible within the time for prototype modification and recruitment resources.
Include only the minimum functionality required to compare primary design assumptions in the scope of the formative evaluation prototype.
The user's iterative design plan can be judged feasible only if time and personnel are allocated for modifying the prototype between iterations.
Delays in participant recruitment can compress the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.
Use an em dash only for a deliberate interruption or sharp contrast; otherwise split the sentence or choose ordinary punctuation.
In procedural passages, begin each sentence with the action, condition, or output instead of repeating “we” so the steps remain easy to follow and reuse.
Write system behaviors confirmed in the actual usage environment as observed states.
Write system behaviors not yet confirmed in the field as conditional plans.
Readers can reconstruct a sequence more accurately when each sentence begins with the action or condition rather than the author.
Do not mechanically split connected thoughts into separate short sentences when doing so destroys the intended reading rhythm.
Preserve a longer sentence when its clauses form one continuous movement that is easier to follow together than apart.
The user understands that short sentences are easier to scan but feels that uniformly segmented prose loses its reading rhythm.
Write procedural sentences so their opening phrase can be reused as a checklist item without changing the step's meaning.
The user should choose “I” as an individual author or “we” for a named team and should not mix them when describing the same responsible party.
Action-first procedural sentences can be reordered or copied into a checklist more easily because their subject is the step rather than the proposal author.
The user can explain whether an em dash marks an intentional interruption or contrast rather than using it decoratively.
An em dash creates a stronger interruption than a comma and can make a deliberate contrast easier to hear in the sentence.

analysis.overview: Both frames promote explicit handling of evidentiary status, while otherwise covering independent concerns: the reference emphasizes study feasibility, resource staging, prototype scope, and recruitment risk; the compared frame emphasizes procedural clarity, sentence rhythm, authorial voice, and deliberate em-dash use.

relations.reason: The reference requires unverified schedule, recruitment, and technical assumptions to be marked, while the compared frame distinguishes observed system states from unconfirmed conditional plans; together they govern explicit representation of evidentiary status without contradiction.
relations.summary: Claims should be expressed according to whether their underlying assumptions or behaviors have been verified.

relations.reason: This stage-specific resource-mapping requirement appears only in the reference frame and is independently useful.
relations.summary: Requested resources should be tied to the prototype-fabrication or user-study stage where they are used.

relations.reason: These reference memories split one underlying feasibility criterion across its three resource inputs, with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Procedure feasibility is judged from assigned personnel, equipment, and time.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim independently governs whether the intended evaluation cycle count is feasible.
relations.summary: The planned number of formative iterations should be checked against modification time and recruitment resources.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim independently constrains prototype scope.
relations.summary: A formative-evaluation prototype should contain only the minimum functionality needed to compare primary design assumptions.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim states a specific feasibility condition for between-iteration modification capacity.
relations.summary: Iterative-design feasibility depends on allocating time and personnel to modify the prototype between iterations.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim identifies a distinct schedule dependency and risk mechanism.
relations.summary: Participant-recruitment delays can reduce the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.

relations.reason: The compared memories state one underlying punctuation policy together with its interpretive test and rationale, absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Em dashes should mark intentional interruption or sharp contrast, reflecting their stronger audible break rather than serving as decoration.

relations.reason: The compared memories restate and explain one action-first procedural-writing policy, with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Procedural sentences should begin with the action, condition, or output so sequences remain clear and steps can be reused or reordered as checklist items.

relations.reason: The compared memories express one underlying preference against uniformly short, rhythm-breaking prose, absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Connected clauses should remain together when mechanical segmentation would damage an otherwise clearer continuous reading rhythm.

relations.reason: This compared-only claim independently governs authorial voice and responsibility attribution.
relations.summary: Descriptions of one responsible party should consistently use either “I” for an individual or “we” for a named team.

reports.both: Both frames distinguish supported claims from unverified or unconfirmed ones and call for wording that makes that status explicit.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers action-first reusable procedures, deliberate em-dash use, preservation of sentence rhythm, and consistent authorial pronouns.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers resource-to-stage mapping, procedure-level feasibility, iteration and modification capacity, minimal prototype scope, and recruitment-delay risk.
